explanation: King of Judah who was crowned at a young age and did what was right in the Lord's eyes under the guidance of priest Jehoiada.
A high priest in Jerusalem who helped Joash restore the temple and maintain justice in the land.
A holy place in Jerusalem built by King Solomon to worship God and house the Ark of the Covenant.
A Canaanite god, often worshipped by Israelites despite God's warnings.
A Hebrew word meaning "hosts" or "armies," often used in connection with God as a description of his power and authority.
A prophet and son of Jehoiada, who spoke out against idolatry in Judah and was stoned on Joash's orders.
An Egyptian princess who married Joash and gained great influence over him, leading him to turn away from God.
An ancient region in the Middle East whose army invaded Judah and defeated Joash's forces, leaving him wounded and vulnerable to assassination.
